title: All-powerful, all-loving
hookLine: classic attributes: God is almighty, all-knowing, everywhere, and love

lines: FROM WHAT GOD IS NOT, TO WHAT GOD IS.
cards: "I believe in God the Father Almighty, Maker of heaven and earth." In churches that say the Apostles' Creed, a whole room says that line together, some half awake, some meaning every word.

Almighty is one of the first things it says about God. Yesterday was the way of not. Today goes the other way, to the old list of what Christians say God is: almighty, all-knowing, everywhere, and love.
Put the first word next to the last, and things get interesting. Today's word: all-powerful.

teach.b: Christian teachers have long spoken of God's attributes, the things that are true of God. All-powerful: in Genesis, God says to Abram, "I am the Almighty God; walk before me, and be thou perfect."

All-knowing and everywhere come alive in Psalm 139, which sounds less like a textbook than like someone who can't get away. "For there is not a word in my tongue, but, lo, O LORD, thou knowest it altogether."
Then: "Whither shall I go from thy spirit? or whither shall I flee from thy presence?" Heaven, the grave, the far side of the sea: God is there too.

teach.h: THY RIGHT HAND SHALL HOLD ME.
teach.b: And there the psalm turns: "Even there shall thy hand lead me, and thy right hand shall hold me." Being known everywhere stops being surveillance and becomes being held. Then the fourth word.

The first letter of John says it plainly: "He that loveth not knoweth not God; for God is love." Notice the grammar. The Bible calls God almighty, but in this letter love is not just something God has or does.
It's what God is. Some teachers read the whole list through that line: power that serves love, knowledge that loves what it knows, a presence that holds. And honesty matters here.

Put all-powerful beside all-loving, then look at a hospital ward or a news feed, and hard questions appear. Christians have wrestled with them for a long time, and still do. The list doesn't answer every question.
It tells you which word some Christians put first.

how: In churches that use the Apostles' or Nicene Creed, congregations confess God as the Father Almighty, and preaching and hymns often pair God's power with God's love, drawing on Psalm 139 and the first letter of John.

o: almighty, as the creed calls God
ruling the world by fear and force

games.q: the four words — tap the pairs.
p: whither shall I flee from thy presence?

s: Psalm 139 makes being known everywhere sound like surveillance
it turns to comfort: "even there shall thy hand lead me, and thy right hand shall hold me."
the first letter of John says God is love
"he that loveth not knoweth not God; for God is love."

games.q: you're the psalm writer, trying to imagine somewhere God isn't: the far side of the sea. what do you find there?
o: at last, a place God can't reach.
God's hand, leading and holding you.
games.why: "even there shall thy hand lead me, and thy right hand shall hold me." the psalm turns being known everywhere into being held.

practice: On one breath, almighty; on the next, all-knowing; then everywhere; then love; then go round again, slowly.
Notice which word meets you today, and whether any of them unsettles you; both are worth noticing, and you don't have to explain why. If you pray, rest on the word that met you and stay with it.

wordCard.voice: All-powerful. Almighty, as the creed says, and in the first letter of John, held together with the line God is love.

orig.note: Greek: the Almighty, ruler of all; a title for God in the creeds and in Revelation.

carryVoice: Your line: god is love first. Power, in this reading, serves love. See you tomorrow.
